row.footnote: Opened in April 1997.  Figures include visitors to Asian Civilisations Museum at Armenian Street (up to December 2005) and Empress Place Building (with effect from March 2003).  With effect from April 2006, Visitorship to the museums is counted using an automatic tracking system, which makes use of tracking devices fixed at all the entrances to the museums.  All visitors who access the museum premises are captured in the count, regardless of whether the entries are based on paid admissions or those not requiring payment.  The place of interest was closed from April to June 2020 due to measures imposed during the global COVID-19 pandemic.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.

Major renovation and repair were carried out during January 1989 to November 1990.  From 28 April 2003 to 6 March 2006, figures refer to Singapore History Museum which was closed and re-opened as National Museum of Singapore (NMS) on 8 December 2006.  From April 2006 to November 2006, exhibitions and fringe activities were held on the premises of NMS.  With effect from April 2006, visitorship to the museums is counted using an automatic tracking system, a device which is fixed at entrances to the museums.  All visitors who access the museum premises are captured in the count, regardless of whether the entries are based on paid admissions or those not requiring payment.  The place of interest was closed from April to June 2020 due to measures imposed during the global COVID-19 pandemic.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.

Opened in January 1996.  With effect from April 2006, visitorship to the museums is counted using an automatic tracking system, a device which is fixed at entrances to the museums.  All visitors who access the museum premises are captured in the count, regardless of whether the entries are based on paid admissions or those not requiring payment.  Visitorship data include visitors to SAM at 8Q which was officially opened on 15 August 2008.  Singapore Art Museum (SAM) had been incorporated as an independent company limited by guarantee in November 2013.  From January 2014, visitorship data are provided by SAM.  SAM at the former St. Joseph's Institution building closed for redevelopment works in September 2018.  Data for 2019 refer to visitorship to SAM at 8Q from 1 January to 28 February 2019.  SAM at 8Q closed for redevelopment in March 2019.  SAM opened its new venue at Tanjong Pagar Distripark in January 2022.  Visitorship from 2022 include visitors to Tanjong Pagar Distripark only.  Data exclude digital visitorship.

Peranakan Museum (PM) was officially opened on 26 April 2008.  Year 2008 data refer to the number of visitors to PM from 26 April 2008 to 31 December 2008.  Visitorship to the museums is counted using an automatic tracking system, which makes use of tracking devices fixed at all the entrances to the museums.  All visitors who access the museum premises are captured in the count, regardless of whether the entries are based on paid admissions or those not requiring payment.  Data for 2019 refer to visitorship to PM from 1 January to 31 March 2019.  PM is closed for redevelopment from 1 April 2019 to 17 Feb 2023.

Data refer to the financial year which begins in April of the current year and ends in March of the following year.  Data from FY2016 to FY2022 includes visitorship to Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC) and SDC's outreach programmes.  Data from FY2023 include visitorship to Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC), SDC's outreach programmes and visitorship to Singapore Navy Museum.  Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC) was closed for renovation from April to October 2020.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.

Figures prior to 1987 refer to financial year from April to March of the following year.  The place of interest was closed from April to June 2020 due to measures imposed during the global COVID-19 pandemic.  From July 2020, Science Centre Singapore is open from Fridays to Sundays, and on School and Public Holidays.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.
Mandai Bird Paradise was officially opened on 8 May 2023.  From 21 April 2023, Mandai Bird Paradise welcomed visitors for preview.

The place of interest was closed from April to June 2020 due to measures imposed during the global COVID-19 pandemic.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.

River Safari was officially opened on 3 April 2013.  The place of interest was closed from April to June 2020 due to measures imposed during the global COVID-19 pandemic.  During periods of heightened alert due to COVID-19, the place of interest operated at a reduced capacity in line with prevailing government guidelines.  It has been renamed as River Wonders wef 13 October 2021.

Year 2024 data refer to visits to Jurong Lake Gardens which includes Lakeside Garden, Chinese Garden and Japanese Garden from September 2024 (opening month) to December 2024.  Data prior to September 2024 refer to visits to Chinese/Japanese Gardens.  From April 2016, data are obtained from National Parks Board.  Prior to April 2016, data were obtained from JTC Corporation.
